Hi,

I'm new to the mirt package and have a clarification question...

If there are missing data in the data file, can fit statistics be calculated?

I'm trying to perform an exploratory item factor analysis on a dataset that has a good deal of missingness. I'm trying to evaluate which model fits the data the best.

Assuming fit statistics cannot be computed in this instance, is my best bet to use AIC and BIC to choose the best fitting model?

Thanks so much for your help!
Hally

On Wed, Sep 7, 2016 at 1:59 PM, <hallyo...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi,

I'm new to the mirt package and have a clarification question...

If there are missing data in the data file, can fit statistics be calculated?
Some can (e.g., itemfits G2 and X2), though unfortunately they aren't the best unless enough information exists to obtain accurate latent trait predictions.

I'm trying to perform an exploratory item factor analysis on a dataset that has a good deal of missingness. I'm trying to evaluate which model fits the data the best.

Assuming fit statistics cannot be computed in this instance, is my best bet to use AIC and BIC to choose the best fitting model?

Yes, AIC is the route you want here because they it is not affected by missing data (BIC unfortunately is due to it's calculated form....which is somewhat contentious). 

Phil

Thanks so much for your help!
Hally
